staff.name: Nora Bennett
staff.view: Protect integration time; separate teams can otherwise commit to incompatible assumptions.

staff.name: James Mercer
staff.view: Ground-test evidence matters more than confidence in an attractive vehicle proposal.

staff.name: Rebecca Hayes
staff.view: Instrument coverage and interfaces must be designed with the mission, not added at the end.

staff.name: Dr Lila Ortiz
staff.view: A successful test supports only the configuration and conditions it actually exercised.

booster.name: Saturn V launch vehicle
booster.description: Propulsion, staging and coupled vehicle dynamics. Existing Saturn IB capability is inherited separately.

designs.name: Tightly integrated vehicle
designs.tradeoff: Lower development commitment; tight payload allowance and more coupled integration work.

designs.name: Interface margin
designs.tradeoff: More time and funding for interface margin; moderate payload allowance.

designs.name: Payload growth allowance
designs.tradeoff: More payload room, but a longer propulsion-development and qualification programme.

csm.name: Command and service module
csm.description: Crew systems, cabin hazards, high-energy entry and return capability.

designs.name: Minimum dry mass
designs.tradeoff: Protects launch mass; dense packaging makes access and cabin integration harder.

designs.name: Service access allowance
designs.tradeoff: More access for inspection and rework, with a larger dry-mass commitment.

designs.name: Separated interfaces
designs.tradeoff: Clearer work-package boundaries; additional interfaces need integrated qualification.

lander.name: Lunar module
lander.description: Independent propulsion, descent/ascent and guidance integration. Requirements depend on the mission architecture.

designs.name: Tight mass allocation
designs.tradeoff: Lower mass and commitment; less installation and integration margin.

designs.name: Maintenance and access allowance
designs.tradeoff: More installation room and access, but a heavier vehicle to launch and land.

designs.name: Modular integration
designs.tradeoff: Longer interface-development programme; work packages are easier to revise independently.

ground.name: Ground systems and crew egress
ground.description: Test classification, isolation, emergency access and the conditions used in occupied ground tests.

designs.name: Shared test installation
designs.tradeoff: Lower facility commitment; shared services require careful isolation and emergency planning.

designs.name: Dedicated occupied-test provision
designs.tradeoff: More capacity tied up in test infrastructure and egress provision.

designs.name: Separate test configurations
designs.tradeoff: More configuration work up front; occupied and unoccupied test interfaces remain distinct.

operations.name: Flight operations and crew preparation
operations.description: Aggregate Mercury/Gemini-derived capability, navigation, rendezvous, procedures and recurring team practice.

designs.name: Concentrated simulation programme
designs.tradeoff: Concentrates resources in simulation; concurrent workload needs careful integration.

designs.name: Distributed rehearsal teams
designs.tradeoff: Broader rehearsal coverage, with greater coordination and staffing commitments.

designs.name: Interface-led operations development
designs.tradeoff: Longer interface and procedure definition before integrated rehearsals.

component.name: Component and procedure tests
component.caveat: Isolated conditions do not qualify coupled flight or occupied ground-test behaviour.

integration.name: Integrated configuration rehearsal
integration.caveat: A ground rehearsal supports this revision under its test conditions; flight evidence is still needed.

missions.name: Apollo 1 / AS-204
missions.objective: Complete occupied ground-test qualification and emergency egress preparation.

missions.name: Apollo 4
missions.objective: Qualify integrated Saturn V flight and high-energy spacecraft entry.

missions.name: Apollo 5
missions.objective: Demonstrate the uncrewed lunar module and its propulsion/control sequence.

missions.name: Apollo 6
missions.objective: Extend integrated booster, dynamic-load and spacecraft qualification.

missions.name: Apollo 7
missions.objective: Demonstrate crewed command/service-module operations in Earth orbit.

missions.name: Apollo 8
missions.objective: Take the crewed spacecraft to lunar orbit and return without an operational LM.

missions.name: Apollo 9
missions.objective: Qualify independent LM flight and crew rendezvous in Earth orbit.

missions.name: Apollo 10
missions.objective: Rehearse lunar descent and rendezvous without landing.

missions.name: Apollo 11
missions.objective: Land, conduct surface work, ascend, rendezvous and return the crew safely.
